verdict.rationale: Context.dev is API-first: every core capability in the evidence (scrape, crawl, extract, screenshots, browser actions, document parsing, monitoring, brand, people and news data) is documented as an API endpoint. A published OpenAPI spec, official SDKs, CLI and MCP server reinforce this, and an agent auth flow lets agents register and obtain tokens programmatically. However, there is no explicit UI/API parity claim, the agent sign-up still needs a browser claim step, and account administration such as API key management reads as dashboard-driven. Missing for 10: an explicit UI/API parity statement, documented API access to account/key/billing management, independent corroboration of parity.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can do everything through the API that I can do in the UI

citations.quote: Scrape websites into Markdown, crawl linked pages, and extract JSON for AI agents and applications.
discover → register → deliver setup link & code to the user → user completes claim in browser → poll for access_token → call API.
PROBE openapi: HTTP 200 at https://docs.context.dev/openapi.json — contains "openapi" key
